BiblicalUsage: Naqat means to loathe, for the soul to be weary of its own life, and its only occurrence is Job at his lowest. In Job 10:1 Job says, my soul is weary of my life, and I will leave my complaint upon myself, and speak in the bitterness of my soul.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Job's weariness is the honest end of suffering without answers, and the Bible does not soften it; He loathes his life and still speaks to God, and that is the prayer.
